channel.title: The Ashgrove Times — The News Desk
channel.description: For the Fellers — the morning paper, filed daily at 7:00 AM ET.

item.title: No. 85 — Tech sell-off erases $1 trillion as Intel posts its worst day
item.description: Nasdaq 100 falls 3.4%, its worst day since June, as investors question returns on AI spending

item.title: No. 84 — Binance says hackers stole $6.3B in largest crypto theft on record
item.description: The exchange halted withdrawals and said about $3B tied to the attackers is frozen; analysts point to North Korea

item.title: No. 83 — Spain's rail toll reaches 68 as minister blames restart order
item.description: Puente says controllers restarted the Renfe train with no speed limit after a signal failure; three days of mourning begin

item.title: No. 82 — Israel's election ends with no majority as Netanyahu bloc leads count
item.description: With 72% counted, Netanyahu's bloc holds 54 seats and Eisenkot's 48; final results are due Friday

item.title: No. 81 — Justice Department charges Comey a third time over 2016 leak
item.description: Prosecutors filed a sealed criminal information to stop a 10-year clock; his lawyers call it time-barred

item.title: No. 80 — Lula wins fourth term as Brazil's president; Bolsonaro rejects result
item.description: Final tally gives Lula 51.8% and a margin of nearly 4.4 million votes; senator seeks to annul the vote

item.title: No. 79 — French police arrest nearly 1,000 as 410,000 march against Macron
item.description: The ministry counts 110,000 in Paris, where masked protesters clashed with riot police; the CGT union counts far more

item.title: No. 78 — US orders diplomats out of Saudi Arabia as military thins Mideast posts
item.description: Houthi strikes on Saudi airports and Iranian threats drive the drawdown; Dammam airport toll rises to two

item.title: No. 77 — Russia frees jailed American teacher as Witkoff meets Putin
item.description: Stephen Hubbard, held since 2022 on mercenary charges, was at a St. Petersburg airport, Putin said

item.title: No. 76 — Alberta votes 76% to stay in Canada, rejecting a separation path
item.description: Smith promises no second vote this mandate; separatists say they will test her hold on the UCP

item.title: No. 75 — Trump defends Russia sanctions waiver, says Zelenskyy wants war to go on
item.description: Bessent declines three times on NBC to call Ukraine an ally; two Republicans seek a Starlink probe

item.title: No. 74 — Explosion and fire at Alberta military base kill soldiers, injure dozens
item.description: Global News puts the toll at 7 dead citing military sources; Edmonton doctor says hospitals are overwhelmed

item.title: No. 73 — Trump waives new Russia sanctions law two days before it took effect
item.description: Waiver halts 100% tariffs on the top buyers of Russian oil and gas; Zelenskyy calls it "unfortunate"

item.title: No. 72 — Gunman kills 3 children and a teacher at Bend, Oregon, elementary school
item.description: A 16-year-old shot through the locked doors of Silver Rail Elementary; a bystander followed and killed him, police said

item.title: No. 71 — Inflation accelerates to 3.7% as gasoline jumps 9.1% in a month
item.description: Core prices climb to 2.6%; markets put odds of an Oct. 28 Fed hike above 55% and the Nasdaq falls 1.8%

item.title: No. 70 — Russian missiles kill 6, cut power to 600,000 despite Trump ceasefire claim
item.description: Zelensky says Kyiv got no warning from partners; adviser says Starlink limits disrupted drone missions

item.title: No. 69 — Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar's home in criminal probe
item.description: Omar calls the search political intimidation; Trump says he had "nothing to do with it"

item.title: No. 68 — Trump declares Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire; Kyiv reports new strikes
item.description: Zelensky says Ukraine learned of the deal from the media; Moscow has not confirmed it

item.title: No. 67 — Riyadh airport attack kills 12; Trump weighs joining war on Houthis
item.description: Saudi aviation authority says 309 wounded and an American among the dead in the deadliest Gulf strike of the Iran war

item.title: No. 66 — Isaias comes ashore at Destin at 105 mph, cuts power to 834,000
item.description: Storm fell to a post-tropical cyclone over Alabama by 4 a.m.; NHC hands off advisories as flood threat moves north

item.title: No. 65 — Isaias strengthens to 110 mph ahead of Gulf Coast landfall tonight
item.description: Mandatory evacuations in two Florida counties and three Alabama beach towns; surge of 5 to 7 feet forecast from Dauphin Island to Indian Pass

item.title: No. 64 — Isaias, season's first hurricane, bears down on the Gulf Coast
item.description: Hurricane warning runs from Ocean Springs, Miss., to Florida's Bay-Gulf county line; two states declare emergencies

item.title: No. 63 — Russian missiles and drones kill at least 11 across Ukraine overnight
item.description: A five-story apartment block in Pryluky was destroyed; Zelensky calls the strike a birthday 'gift' to Putin

item.title: No. 62 — Trump approves firing squad execution for Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
item.description: Pentagon says Hegseth recommended the method; it would be the U.S. military's first execution since 1961

item.title: No. 61 — Flavio Bolsonaro tops Lula in Brazil's first round, forcing runoff
item.description: Senator takes 47.03% to the president's 45.16%, defying polls that had Lula ahead; the second round is Oct. 25

item.title: No. 60 — Latvia's Kulbergs wins record 42 seats in low-turnout election
item.description: United List takes about 35% of Saturday's vote, the most for one party since independence; turnout falls to 51.8%, a record low

item.title: No. 59 — G7 agrees to release 100 million barrels of oil to curb diesel prices
item.description: Four-month drawdown through the International Energy Agency begins at once, with a diesel release front-loaded into the first 20 days

item.title: No. 58 — Crew-13 reaches space station in under eight hours after Cape launch
item.description: Four astronauts dock seven hours, 55 minutes after an 11:10 a.m. liftoff, the quickest SpaceX crew flight yet

item.title: No. 57 — Tennessee fails to execute Christa Pike after two lethal doses
item.description: Gov. Bill Lee halts the state's remaining 2026 execution and orders an outside review of what went wrong

item.title: No. 56 — U.S. ends 12-year Iraq mission as last coalition forces leave Erbil
item.description: Pentagon says Iraqi forces now carry primary responsibility; Baghdad declares a four-day holiday
